verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The display is stated in one declaration, for the physical normalisation: physical_source_plus_remainder (PrimaryFieldAssembly.lean:936) forms the sum and evaluates the covariance of the sum, doubleAverage (fun Y θ => (V Y θ + R Y θ) 0 * (V Y θ + R Y θ) i.succ) = q ^ (-velocityExponent h - 1/2) * T0 i + doubleAverage (covarianceError V R i), where V := sourceField A hdet (physicalOuter h N) (physicalViscosity h N) (chartTarget h q N T0) q x is the Q^{-A}-normalised assembled primary wave (sourceField, :622, the ∑ᶠ over SignedIndex of the per-label actualVelocity) and covarianceError V R i = V₀Rᵢ + R₀Vᵢ + R₀Rᵢ (:415), i.e. the paper's ℬ(W_0, LΣ) + C(LΣ) pointwise; the leading term is physical_source_covariance (:644). Two respects in which that statement is not the display letter for letter, both in the direction of generality: R is an arbitrary continuous field rather than LΣ specifically, so the display is its instance; and the remainder is kept as the single unevaluated term doubleAverage (covarianceError V R i) rather than displayed as Σ + C(LΣ), the evaluation of its cross part to Σ being (7.36) itself, stated by physical_signed_cross_covariance (cited under eq-7.36). The underlying algebra is stated at the paper's own averaging level: the paper's C and B of (7.23) are the double averages ⟨⟨·⟩_θ⟩_Y, which is the Lean's doubleAverage, and averaged_covariance_expansion (:456) is the expansion there, doubleAverage of the product of the sum = doubleAverage (V₀Vᵢ) + doubleAverage (covarianceError V R i), with the continuity side conditions discharged inside its own proof. At the angular-mean-only level (CorrectionState.bilinearCovariance = angularAverage of the product, CorrectionState.lean:76-77) the same algebra is covariance_increment_exact (LabelSumBounds.lean:1053), C(u+v) - C(u) = B(u,v) + C(v) for arbitrary u and v — listed as `implies` because that is what it states, the generic expansion and not this display — with the symmetrised cross term carrying its own name, LabelSumBounds.symmetricCovariance u v = bilinearCovariance u v + bilinearCovariance v u (:745), the paper's ℬ; SignedMeanGain.covariance_increment_split (SignedMeanGain.lean:154) repackages it as covarianceIncrement u (t + k) = symmetricCovariance p t + signedRemainder p u t k, where covarianceIncrement u w = bilinearCovariance (u+w) (u+w) - bilinearCovariance u u (:150), its proof being covariance_increment_exact followed by `abel`, signedRemainder (LabelSumBounds.lean:749) being defined to carry the remaining terms with symmetricCovariance p t subtracted back off. The three terms are also evaluated separately, and all three at the same assembled level — a ∑ᶠ over the whole label set of the same shape — so that they conjoin: (i) the primary diagonal term εT_{0,*}, by assembled_covariance, doubleAverage (assembledRadial * assembledTangent) = ∑ᶠ U, outer U ^ 2 * ε U * mask ^ 2 * T U i, whose physical instance physical_primary_covariance evaluates that sum to q ^ (-velocityExponent h - 1/2) * T0 i (PairData.diagonal_pair_reconstruct is the per-label ingredient of the same identity); (ii) the cross term, the paper's Σ, by assembled_cross_covariance, = ∑ᶠ U, outer U ^ 2 * ε U * mask ^ 2 * R U i, whose per-label literal form is cross_reconstruct_component, 2·H(a ⊙ δa) = R; (iii) the signed square C(LΣ), by assembled_signed_square, which is deliberately retained as a separate term rather than absorbed. One qualification, applying equally to the diagonal term and to the cross term: each of these assembled statements carries the same outer rescaling (outer U)^2 = Q^{-2A} and the same squared partition factor mask², so the paper's bare εT_{0,*} and bare Σ are recovered once the physical normalisation of (7.35) is divided out and the squared mask is summed over the tail; that collapse is carried out for the diagonal term by physical_primary_covariance and for the cross term by physical_signed_cross_covariance, which reaches σ i exactly. The same conjunction is available in the chart normalisation, at the meanBar level, where meanBar ∘ bilinearCovariance is again the paper's double average (mean_tangentCovariance_factor, ActualPrimaryCovariance.lean:597-602, changes it to doubleAverage): there the diagonal term is evaluated by mean_tangentCovariance_eq_leading (:614), meanBar (tangentCovariance B N0 0 i.succ) n x = leadingStress i n x for n ≥ (choice B N0).prepared.N + 1 and x in the native strip, and the cross term in the same type and the same normalisation is requested_cross_tail (cited under eq-7.36), so that route conjoins with no rescaling step in between.
